scope: Actual visual inspection of eight final full-world unfiltered Adler PNGs: day/night exterior and show bookmarks, plus gallery and show40/100/179s phases. No rendering or source changes were performed during review.

images.label: day exterior
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: The west entrance, broad stair, railings, three receding roof rings and warm copper dome are fully in frame.
The glass crescent and its radial framing extend to both sides; the approach paving is visible in the foreground.
No camera obstruction, broken shell or bright seam is visible.
limitations: Trees and broad facade surfaces remain stylized architectural geometry; this is not photographic reproduction.

images.label: night exterior
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: Warm facade pools, bright entrance trim and the lower copper dome are readable against the dark sky.
The upper landing, some tread edges and central handrail are visible; light reflects on the foreground paving.
The upper copper apex remains dark, consistent with the documented evening-lighting balance.
limitations: Most of the lower stair run remains very dim; this image does not support a claim that every tread is brightly illuminated.
Fine stochastic grain remains in dark paving and reflected highlights in this unfiltered still.

images.label: day show bookmark
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: A complete ringed planet is centered amid teal/purple bands, white stars and blue line constellations.
Seating blocks and the central aisle form dark foreground silhouettes without blocking the main display.
No narrow bright polar wedges or shell light leaks are visible.
limitations: The display is deliberately artistic, and bright peripheral stars appear softly elliptical in the wide view.
Seat details remain low contrast in the dark room.

images.label: night show bookmark
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: The same centered planet and colored dome composition remain readable in night mode.
The central aisle and seat silhouettes remain clear of the projected centerpiece.
No bright top-edge slivers or projection showing through an exterior backing are visible.
limitations: Dark seats are visible principally as silhouettes; no claim of evenly lit upholstery is made.

images.label: gallery at65s
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: A ringed-planet exhibit and telescope stand on lit plinths beside the glazed crescent.
The tiled circulation floor is visible and clear ahead; the opaque theater backing occupies the right side.
No stars bleed through that backing, and there is no camera penetration or obvious clipped exhibit.
limitations: Some ceiling and window-shadow regions retain sampling grain.
The gallery and exhibits are original interpretations rather than a survey of current operational installations.

images.label: show at40s
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: Teal and purple bands sweep across the dome, with line constellations and varying stars visible.
The large moving planet is partly beyond the upper-right edge; the room and central aisle remain visible below.
No top-edge triangular polar slivers are visible.
limitations: This selected direction does not contain the entire moving planet; the show occupies more of the dome than the camera field of view.

images.label: show at100s
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: The pole region and upper image edge have regular soft star points without the previously identified narrow bright slivers.
Colored bands span the lower dome and the dark constellation lines remain visible above them.
Seat blocks and the aisle are visible; no foreground geometry blocks the main sky field.
limitations: This still verifies the previously affected composition only; it does not establish all-frame temporal stability.

images.label: show at179s
images.viewMethod: view_image full frame, no exposure or color edits
observations: The ringed planet has returned near the center, with teal on the left and purple on the right, close to the opening composition.
The seat arrangement and aisle remain aligned with the opening view.
No late-program blank screen, bright polar wedges or unexpected camera obstruction are visible.
limitations: 179s is near the loop endpoint; this image alone does not establish exact camera or image equality at180s.

polarCorrection: The actual100s composition that previously exposed top-edge wedges was viewed again; those bright slivers are absent. The other sampled dome compositions are also clean.
entranceLighting: Doorway, upper landing and central rail are readable; lower stairs remain dim. This is a bounded practical-light improvement, not uniform stair floodlighting.
limits: This is a sampled still-image review, not a full movie, full-route collision test or proof that all interactive motion is noise-free.
The unfiltered stills retain some stochastic noise on dark surfaces. Motion reconstruction quality is measured by the separate paired full-world GPU suite.
The original show is an artistic silent composition; no astronomy or operational-gallery accuracy is inferred from its visual appearance.
renderRevision: Reviewed images precede the later Shedd context and first-camera correction; the Adler geometry and shaders are unchanged. Exact old images are preserved at the archived paths.
